exceptions.title: Vendor contract without a breach-notice clause (V-06, Harbor HRIS)
exceptions.plain: The contract with the payroll and employee-records vendor does not say how fast it must tell Nimbus about a breach. The gap is written down with an end date while the clause is negotiated.
exceptions.reason: The Harbor HRIS agreement (V-06) was signed on the vendor's standard paper before the clause checklist existed. It has no breach notification window and no subprocessor change notice. The vendor has agreed in principle to a 72-hour clause at the renewal in early 2027; until then the control is partial for this one vendor.
exceptions.compensating: Quarterly vendor status and security bulletin monitoring (NC-DE-03) with the vendor's incident page checked at each review; data minimization: the system holds staff records only and no customer data, and export access is limited to two named roles; the breach notification procedure (NC-RS-03) treats any vendor report as day zero so the Texas clocks can still be met.

exceptions.title: Standing model API key instead of a short-lived workload identity
exceptions.plain: The key that lets the assistants call the AI model is a long-lived key that a person changes by hand, rather than a key the platform issues fresh for each job. It is protected in other ways until that is fixed.
exceptions.reason: The AI assistants and the control mapper call the model provider with a standing API key stored as a platform environment variable and rotated manually. A short-lived workload identity issued by the hosting platform is the target state, but the current hosting and provider combination does not offer it without a proxy service that would add a new component to maintain.
exceptions.compensating: The key is referenced only by server-side code and never shipped to the browser (NC-PR-04); the repository is secret-scanned on every build and daily; public endpoints enforce a per-visitor rate limit, a daily cap and input length caps that bound the spend even if the key is misused through the site (NC-PR-10); the kill switch removes the key and redeploys within 15 minutes (NC-PR-19); rotation is logged in the non-human identity inventory with a 90-day interval while the exception is open.

exceptions.title: Shadow AI discovery runs quarterly, not continuously
exceptions.plain: Nimbus checks every three months for AI tools staff have started using without approval. A continuous check would catch a slip within days instead of weeks, and that has not been bought yet.
exceptions.reason: Discovery of unapproved AI services relies on the quarterly review of expense reports and browser-extension inventories. A software discovery and data-loss-prevention subscription would make this continuous, but it needs budget and an integration with the identity provider; the board decision is tracked under R-09.
exceptions.compensating: AI use policy with prohibited uses and an approval path (NC-GV-07); annual awareness training that covers pasting customer data into outside tools (NC-GV-06); an approved tool list in the AI inventory (NC-GV-08); the data inventory marks which classes may never leave company systems (NC-ID-02); the quarterly review is recorded with findings and removals.

exceptions.title: No server-side aggregation of AI assistant metrics, by privacy design
exceptions.plain: The assistants show their own answer, refusal and hand-off counts on the page, but Nimbus does not collect those numbers centrally, because doing so would mean recording something about each conversation. Attack testing covers the gap for now.
exceptions.reason: The public assistants process conversations in memory only and store no transcripts (NC-PR-14). Session metrics are computed in the visitor's browser and are not sent to a server, so the monthly drift review works from test runs rather than production aggregates. Adding a privacy-preserving counter (counts only, no content) is planned but has not been designed or reviewed yet.
exceptions.compensating: Adversarial testing before release and after any model change, covering prompt injection, false authority, policy abuse, data exfiltration and phantom action claims (NC-DE-05); a public findings register with a gate per finding (NC-ID-06); the monthly review runs the gold-set evaluation and the endpoint gate against the live model as a proxy for drift (NC-PR-20).
